chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who struck a gazelle with his sword until he skinned it, is it permissible to eat it? He said: 'Yes, he may eat from the part near the head and leave the tail.'
ai.seo_question: What part of a hunted gazelle is permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of consuming wild game hunted by a Muslim, specifically addressing the gazelle. The ruling distinguishes between permissible meat and the tail, reflecting the detailed jurisprudential approach to *dhaba’ih* (slaughter/consumption) of wild animals in Shia fiqh, where the method of killing determines edibility.
